Steady evening at the staff meeting
Attendees heard from the welfare lead
Andre Williams, Layla Johnson, and Winston were present, along with the senior coordinator, the desk lead, and the welfare lead.

The desk opened with a quick review of animal comfort handling and the handoff points between check-in and cabin support. The team agreed that safety stays ahead of speed on every journey, and that any sign of stress in a pet gets flagged fast. Notes were made on crate fit, water checks, and the way staff should speak to travelers so the whole process feels calm and clear. The group also picked up on a few service changes that need to be logged right away in the desk ledger, since clean records keep the next shift from guessing.

The welfare lead asked for tighter follow-through when travelers arrive with extra care needs. <<FACT F085>> The room kept the tone practical, and the desk lead said staff should keep using the same calm language at every handoff so the passenger side and the animal side stay aligned. There was also a short run-through of how to handle busy boarding periods without crowding the animal area or letting paperwork slip.

Andre Williams and Layla Johnson were noted in the discussion as examples of how good coordination helps avoid delay. Winston came up as a reminder that small comfort details matter, especially when a pet is uneasy or tired. The group closed the loop on who checks the carrier tags, who confirms the comfort setup, and who updates the ledger if anything changes after the first review.

Aurelia Skyways will keep the current routine in place, with the senior coordinator watching for repeat issues and the welfare lead collecting feedback from the floor. The meeting ended with no major concerns left open, and the team moved out with clear next steps.
